name: Testosterone
route_note: IM esters every 1–3 weeks or every 10–14 weeks (undecanoate); daily transdermal gel or patch; oral undecanoate capsules; SC autoinjector; nasal gel; implanted pellets

discovery.by: Ernst Laqueur (isolation, Organon); Adolf Butenandt and Leopold Ruzicka (synthesis)
discovery.note: Isolated from bull testes in 1935 and synthesised the same year; Butenandt and Ruzicka shared the 1939 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

tagline: The principal male sex hormone, used for hypogonadism and gender-affirming care
summary: Testosterone is the main male sex hormone and is used as replacement therapy for male hypogonadism, in delayed puberty and in gender-affirming treatment. It is given by injection, skin gel, oral capsule, nasal gel or implant; it is a controlled substance in the US because of misuse as an anabolic steroid.
mechanism: Testosterone binds the intracellular androgen receptor, which acts as a ligand-activated transcription factor. In tissues such as prostate, skin and hair follicles, 5α-reductase converts it to the more potent dihydrotestosterone; aromatase converts part of it to estradiol, which mediates effects on bone and other tissues.

Androgen receptor activation develops and maintains male sexual characteristics, spermatogenesis (with FSH), libido, muscle mass, erythropoiesis and bone density. Exogenous testosterone suppresses pituitary LH and FSH, reducing endogenous production and sperm output.
uses: Gender-affirming hormone therapy for transgender men (off-label in many labels)

history.title: Isolation and synthesis
history.detail: Laqueur's group isolates testosterone; Butenandt and Ruzicka independently synthesise it.

history.title: Nobel Prize
history.detail: Butenandt and Ruzicka receive the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work on sex hormones.

history.title: US controlled substance
history.detail: Under the Anabolic Steroids Control Act of 1990, testosterone becomes a Schedule III drug.

history.title: AndroGel
history.detail: FDA approves AndroGel, a transdermal gel that greatly expands testosterone prescribing.

history.title: Secondary exposure warning
history.detail: FDA adds a boxed warning about virilisation of children exposed to testosterone gels.

history.title: Labelling on age-related low testosterone
history.detail: FDA requires labels to state that benefit for age-related hypogonadism is not established and to mention possible cardiovascular risk.

history.title: Oral undecanoate
history.detail: FDA approves Jatenzo, an oral testosterone undecanoate capsule.

history.title: TRAVERSE trial
history.detail: TRAVERSE finds testosterone non-inferior to placebo for major cardiovascular events in hypogonadal men at high CV risk.

history.title: Class labelling update
history.detail: FDA requires class-wide labelling changes reflecting TRAVERSE, retaining blood-pressure warnings.

pk.half_life: 10–100 min (free); ester-dependent depot duration of days to weeks
pk.bioavailability: low orally unless as lymphatically absorbed undecanoate; about 10% of gel dose absorbed
pk.metabolism: hepatic; also converted to DHT (5α-reductase) and estradiol (aromatase)
pk.excretion: urine as glucuronide and sulfate conjugates

serious: virilisation of women and children exposed to gel
safety.boxed_warning: Topical gels/solutions: secondary exposure can cause virilisation in children. Some products (Xyosted, Jatenzo, Tlando, Kyzatrex): blood-pressure increases that can raise cardiovascular risk. Aveed: pulmonary oil microembolism and anaphylaxis.

facts: Testosterone has been a US Schedule III controlled substance since 1991.
Butenandt was forced by the Nazi government to decline the 1939 Nobel Prize and received it after the war.
